test_cases.test_name: SPC Dashboard Data Import and Chart Creation Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify the system can successfully import data from CSV files and create X-bar/R and p-charts using vendor standard functionality
prerequisites: SPC dashboard installed and configured
Test CSV files with sample QC data prepared
User account with appropriate permissions

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using valid credentials
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and dashboard main interface is displayed

test_steps.action: Navigate to data import section and select CSV import option
test_steps.expected_result: CSV import interface is displayed with file selection options

test_steps.action: Upload prepared test CSV file containing QC data points
test_steps.expected_result: File upload completes successfully and data validation occurs

test_steps.action: Select X-bar/R chart creation option from the dashboard menu
test_steps.expected_result: X-bar/R chart is generated using the imported data with proper calculations

test_steps.action: Repeat chart creation process for p-chart using the same dataset
test_steps.expected_result: P-chart is successfully generated with appropriate proportion calculations

acceptance_criteria: CSV files import successfully without errors
X-bar/R and p-charts render correctly
Statistical calculations match expected values
All chart elements display properly
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements
GAMP 5 guidelines for standard software validation
data_integrity_requirements: Imported data must maintain original values without alteration
Chart calculations must be mathematically accurate
All data transformations must be traceable

test_cases.test_name: Nelson Rules Application and Export Functionality Test
test_cases.objective: Verify the system correctly applies vendor standard Nelson rules to control charts and exports results to PDF/CSV formats
prerequisites: SPC dashboard with imported test data
Charts created from test data
User account with export permissions

test_steps.action: Open previously created X-bar/R chart in the dashboard
test_steps.expected_result: Chart displays with all data points and control limits visible

test_steps.action: Enable Nelson rules application from the chart options menu
test_steps.expected_result: Nelson rules are applied and violations are highlighted on the chart

test_steps.action: Verify each Nelson rule is correctly identifying appropriate patterns
test_steps.expected_result: All eight Nelson rules are functioning according to vendor specifications

test_steps.action: Select PDF export option from the export menu
test_steps.expected_result: PDF export dialog appears with configuration options

test_steps.action: Export chart with Nelson rules applied to PDF format
test_steps.expected_result: PDF file is generated containing the chart with Nelson rule violations marked

test_steps.action: Repeat export process for CSV format with statistical data
test_steps.expected_result: CSV file is generated containing numerical data and rule violation flags

acceptance_criteria: Nelson rules are correctly applied according to vendor specifications
PDF exports contain accurate chart representations
CSV exports contain complete numerical data
All rule violations are properly flagged in exports
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signatures requirements
FDA guidance on process validation
GAMP Category 3 software validation principles
data_integrity_requirements: Nelson rule calculations must be mathematically correct
Exported files must preserve original data integrity
Rule violation flags must be accurately represented in exports

test_cases.test_name: Control Chart Creation and Nelson Rules Application
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can correctly create X-bar/R and p-charts from CSV data and apply the vendor's standard Nelson rules for statistical process control.
prerequisites: Valid user account with chart creation permissions
Test CSV files containing sample QC data for X-bar/R and p-charts
SPC dashboard application is installed and accessible

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard with a valid user account that has chart creation permissions.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and is presented with the main dashboard interface.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the main dashboard after login

test_steps.action: Navigate to the chart creation module and select the option to create a new X-bar/R chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the interface for uploading data and configuring the X-bar/R chart.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the X-bar/R chart creation interface

test_steps.action: Upload the provided test CSV file containing variable data suitable for an X-bar/R chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully loads the CSV data and displays a preview or summary of the imported data points.
data_to_capture: Log message confirming successful data import

test_steps.action: Configure the chart settings as required and enable the vendor's standard Nelson rules for the chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The chart is generated with control limits calculated, and Nelson rules are activated and visible in the chart settings.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the final X-bar/R chart with control limits
Screenshot of the Nelson rules configuration being enabled

test_steps.action: Repeat steps 2-4 to create a p-chart using a test CSV file containing attribute data.
test_steps.expected_result: A p-chart is successfully generated with control limits and Nelson rules applied.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the final p-chart with control limits

test_steps.action: Verify that the Nelson rules correctly flag data points that violate the statistical rules on both chart types.
test_steps.expected_result: The system visually highlights or annotates data points that trigger any of the Nelson rules on both the X-bar/R and p-charts.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of a chart showing a flagged data point based on a Nelson rule

acceptance_criteria: X-bar/R and p-charts are successfully created from the provided CSV files
Vendor standard Nelson rules are correctly applied and visually indicated on the charts
Control limits are calculated accurately based on the imported data
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and automated processes in QC
ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management principles for statistical process control
data_integrity_requirements: Imported CSV data must be accurately represented in the charts without alteration
Chart configurations and rule applications must be consistent and reproducible

test_cases.test_name: Data Export and Report Scheduling Functionality
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system can export charts and data to PDF and CSV formats and successfully schedule automated report emails using the vendor's scheduler.
prerequisites: Valid user account with export and scheduling permissions
A pre-configured control chart (from OQ-003)
Access to a test email account for receiving scheduled reports

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard with a valid user account that has export and scheduling permissions.
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and can access the pre-configured chart from the previous test.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the dashboard showing the accessible chart

test_steps.action: Select the pre-configured X-bar/R chart and use the export function to save it as a PDF file.
test_steps.expected_result: The system generates a PDF file containing the chart image and relevant statistical data.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the export confirmation message

test_steps.action: Export the underlying chart data to a CSV file using the system's export functionality.
test_steps.expected_result: A CSV file is generated containing the raw data points and calculated control limits used in the chart.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the export confirmation message

test_steps.action: Navigate to the report scheduling module and configure a new scheduled email report for the p-chart.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the scheduling interface allowing configuration of frequency, recipients, and report content.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the scheduling configuration interface

test_steps.action: Set up a one-time immediate test email to the designated test email account, attaching both PDF and CSV formats of the p-chart report.
test_steps.expected_result: The system confirms the schedule and processes the immediate email request.
data_to_capture: Timestamp of when the email was sent

test_steps.action: Verify that the test email account receives the scheduled report with the correct attachments.
test_steps.expected_result: The email is delivered successfully with both PDF and CSV attachments that match the exported files from steps 2 and 3.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the received email with attachments
Verification that attachment contents are correct

acceptance_criteria: Charts and data can be successfully exported to both PDF and CSV formats
The vendor scheduler correctly sends automated report emails with the specified attachments
Exported files maintain data integrity and are readable in standard applications
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records and signatures
ALCOA+ principles for data integrity in exported records
data_integrity_requirements: Exported data must be complete and accurate compared to the source data in the system
Scheduled reports must be delivered reliably with intact attachments

test_cases.test_name: ODBC Data Import and Chart Generation Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify the system can successfully import data from an ODBC data source and generate accurate control charts from the imported data.
prerequisites: ODBC data source configured with test data
Valid user credentials with import permissions
ODBC connector installed and configured

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section and select ODBC as the import source
test_steps.expected_result: System displays ODBC connection configuration options

test_steps.action: Configure ODBC connection parameters and connect to the test database
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully establishes connection to ODBC data source

test_steps.action: Select appropriate data table and map columns to chart variables
test_steps.expected_result: System displays data preview with correct column mapping

test_steps.action: Import data and generate X-bar/R chart from the ODBC source
test_steps.expected_result: System successfully imports data and renders control chart within 2 seconds

acceptance_criteria: ODBC connection established successfully
Data imported without errors
Control chart rendered within 2 seconds
Chart displays correct statistical calculations
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 compliance for electronic records
Data integrity ALCOA+ principles
data_integrity_requirements: Data must maintain accuracy and completeness during transfer
Audit trail must record data import actions if supported
urs_requirements: URS-020-012: Import data from CSV and ODBC connections using standard connectors

test_cases.objective: Verify the system can successfully schedule and automatically email reports to designated recipients using the vendor scheduler.
prerequisites: Email server configured in system settings
Test email accounts configured
Report template created and saved
User with scheduling permissions

test_steps.action: Navigate to report scheduling section and create new scheduled report
test_steps.expected_result: System displays scheduling configuration options

test_steps.action: Configure report schedule (daily at specific time), recipient list, and report format (PDF)
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts scheduling parameters without errors

test_steps.action: Save schedule and verify it appears in the scheduled tasks list
test_steps.expected_result: System confirms schedule creation and displays it in active schedules

test_steps.action: Wait for scheduled time or manually trigger immediate execution
test_steps.expected_result: System processes and sends report at scheduled time

test_steps.action: Verify recipients received email with correct PDF attachment
test_steps.expected_result: Email delivered successfully with proper formatting and attachment

acceptance_criteria: Report schedule created successfully
Email delivered to all recipients
PDF attachment contains correct data
Process completes within expected timeframes
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature requirements
Data integrity requirements for automated processes
data_integrity_requirements: Scheduled reports must maintain data accuracy
Email distribution must be reliable and complete
Audit trail of scheduled executions if supported
urs_requirements: URS-020-006: The system shall support scheduled report emails using vendor scheduler
URS-020-003: The system shall provide vendor standard export to PDF

test_cases.objective: Verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully schedule and send automated reports via email using the vendor's scheduler functionality.
prerequisites: SPC dashboard installed and configured
Valid email server configuration
Test email accounts configured
Sample dataset loaded

test_steps.action: Navigate to the scheduling module and configure a new report schedule with specific time and frequency
test_steps.expected_result: Schedule configuration interface loads successfully and accepts input parameters

test_steps.action: Select a standard report template and configure email recipients for the scheduled report
test_steps.expected_result: Report template selection and recipient configuration are successfully saved

test_steps.action: Trigger the scheduled report manually or wait for scheduled time and verify email delivery
test_steps.expected_result: Report is generated and email is successfully delivered to all configured recipients

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled reports are generated according to configured schedule
Emails are delivered to all specified recipients
Report content matches the selected template format
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements
GMP documentation practices
data_integrity_requirements: Email distribution records must be maintained
Report content must be consistent with source data

test_cases.test_name: Large Dataset Performance and Rendering Test
test_cases.objective: Verify that the SPC dashboard meets performance requirements when loading and rendering large datasets with 100k+ data points.
prerequisites: SPC dashboard installed on supported hardware
Test dataset with 100,000+ data points prepared
Performance monitoring tools available

test_steps.action: Import the large test dataset (100k+ points) via CSV import functionality
test_steps.expected_result: Dataset is successfully imported without errors

test_steps.action: Initiate rendering of X-bar/R chart using the imported large dataset
test_steps.expected_result: Chart renders successfully with all data points processed
data_to_capture: Visual verification of complete dataset representation

test_steps.action: Apply filter changes to the chart and measure re-rendering performance
test_steps.expected_result: Chart re-renders quickly after filter application with updated data display

acceptance_criteria: Dataset of 100k+ points loads in under 5 seconds
Charts render in under 2 seconds after filter changes
No system crashes or performance degradation observed
regulatory_basis: FDA guidance on computerized system performance
GAMP5 performance verification requirements
data_integrity_requirements: All data points must be accurately represented in charts
No data loss during large dataset operations

test_cases.test_name: ODBC Data Source Integration and Import Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully connect to and import data from a configured ODBC data source using the vendor's standard connectors.
prerequisites: OQ-001 (Installation Verification) must be executed and passed
A test database with a configured ODBC System DSN is available
Test dataset containing at least 1000 records of QC data is loaded in the test database
User account with data import permissions is available

test_steps.action: Launch the SPC dashboard and navigate to the data import section.
test_steps.expected_result: Dashboard loads successfully and data import options are displayed.

test_steps.action: Select the ODBC import option and choose the pre-configured test data source from the list.
test_steps.expected_result: System displays available ODBC data sources and allows selection of the test DSN.

test_steps.action: Configure the import settings to map database columns to SPC chart variables and execute the import.
test_steps.expected_result: Data mapping interface is functional and import process completes without errors.

test_steps.action: Verify the imported data by creating a basic X-bar chart using the ODBC-sourced data.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart renders correctly using the imported data, confirming successful integration.

acceptance_criteria: ODBC connection is established successfully within 30 seconds
All test records are imported without data corruption or loss
Imported data is accurately represented in the generated control chart
No system crashes or unhandled exceptions occur during the process
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records integrity
GAMP 5 guidelines for configuration of standard software
data_integrity_requirements: Data transferred via ODBC must maintain accuracy and completeness
Import process must not alter source data values
Audit trail must record the data source and import timestamp if supported
urs_requirements: URS-020-012: Import data from CSV and ODBC connections using standard connectors

test_cases.test_name: Scheduled Report Generation and Email Distribution Test
test_cases.objective: To verify that the vendor's built-in scheduler can automatically generate and email reports according to a predefined schedule.
prerequisites: OQ-003 (Basic Chart Functionality) must be executed and passed
A test email account is configured for receiving reports
A pre-configured report template with sample data is available
Scheduling feature is enabled in the application

test_steps.action: Access the scheduling module and create a new scheduled report job for immediate execution.
test_steps.expected_result: Scheduling interface loads and allows configuration of report parameters and timing.

test_steps.action: Configure the report to generate a PDF export of a control chart and send to the test email address.
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts email configuration and report format selection without errors.

test_steps.action: Save the scheduled job and manually trigger immediate execution for testing purposes.
test_steps.expected_result: Job is saved successfully and immediate execution command is accepted.

test_steps.action: Monitor the system for report generation and verify email delivery to the test account.
test_steps.expected_result: Report is generated within specified time limits and email is delivered successfully.

test_steps.action: Verify the received report for completeness and accuracy compared to on-screen display.
test_steps.expected_result: Exported report matches the on-screen chart display in content and formatting.

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled report generates within 2 minutes of trigger time
Email is delivered to the specified recipient with correct attachment
Exported PDF report contains all chart elements and data points accurately
Scheduler maintains job configuration after system restart
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for automated processes and electronic records
GMP requirements for automated reporting systems
data_integrity_requirements: Scheduled reports must maintain data accuracy identical to manual exports
Email distribution must not alter report content
Scheduler must log execution attempts and outcomes
urs_requirements: URS-020-003: The system shall provide vendor standard export to PDF and CSV
URS-020-006: The system shall support scheduled report emails using vendor scheduler
